family.name: Product Analyst / Associate PM
family.summary: An A/B test the PM wants to ship on Monday: spot the broken user split and the revenue the headline hides, decide what to recommend, and catch a correlation passed off as cause.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Is this a win?
stages.summary: Read an A/B test with a broken 50/50 split, revenue per user that falls, and a short test over a sale weekend. Think aloud.

stages.title: Your recommendation
stages.summary: Commit to a recommendation with the PM pushing to ship. Think aloud.

stages.title: What happens next
stages.summary: The consequences of their recommendation. Tests adapting and owning the call.

stages.title: Review a teammate's analysis
stages.summary: An analysis that treats a correlation as cause, uses a skewed average and a misleading chart. Think aloud.

stages.title: Write the readout (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the experiment readout for the PM with AI. Catches over-claiming from a p-value.

stages.title: An analysis that changed a decision
stages.summary: A real analysis that changed what a team did. Checks specificity and ownership.

brief.text: You're the product analyst at **Bookmyroom**, a hotel booking app. The team tested showing the total price with taxes on the search results page. Users were meant to be split **50/50** at random. The test ran for 4 days, Friday to Monday; Saturday was a site-wide sale.
The PM writes: "Conversion is up and it's significant. Let's ship it to everyone on Monday."
The company and numbers are fictional, and every candidate gets a slightly different version. A calculator is fine.

prompt.text: Tell us about a chart or statistic in the news that you didn’t trust, and why.
Keep it under 45 seconds. This one is not scored; it just gets you talking.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **What do you tell the PM?** Say what in the dashboard worries you, and what you would check before anyone ships.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

choices.label: Fix the split and re-run it for two full weeks
Ship it to 50% of users and keep watching
Stop the test and drop the change

prompt.text: **What do you recommend?** Pick one, then give the two sentences you would say to the PM.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Ship it to everyone now"

prompt.text: Two weeks after shipping, revenue is down slightly and support reports that showing the total price with taxes on the search results page is broken on older Android phones (7% of users). Finance asks whether the test "proved" it would work.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Fix the split and re-run it for two full weeks"

prompt.text: Engineering found the cause: on older Android phones the variant page failed to load, so those users fell out. After the fix, the re-run shows conversion +1.8% (p = 0.21) and revenue per user flat. The PM asks: "So is it a yes or a no?"
**What do you say?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Ship it to 50% of users and keep watching"

prompt.text: A week later the 50% rollout "looks good" on the dashboard, but the user split is still uneven, and two other teams have started a test on the same page.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Stop the test and drop the change"

prompt.text: The PM is frustrated: "We spent a sprint on this and you killed it on a technicality." The designer asks whether the idea itself was wrong.
**What do you say and do?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: A teammate wants to present this to leadership. **Name the three biggest problems, worst first, and what each could lead leadership to do wrong.**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

items: Users who used price alerts had 59% 90-day retention, against 22% for everyone else. **price alerts more than doubles retention.**
10% of users have used it. Recommendation: make price alerts the first screen for every new user to double retention.
Average session length for these users: 18 minutes.
Chart: retention by month, y-axis from 40% to 60%.
Based on 6 months of data and over 200,000 users.

prompt.text: Use any AI tool you like for this one. We are assessing how you use it, not whether you do.
Write the readout of the original four-day test for the PM and designer (under 200 words): what was tested, what the data shows, what it doesn't show, and the recommendation.

items: Paste your full AI conversation, or write "none".
In 2–3 lines, say what you kept, changed or rejected from the AI and why.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

stages.title: An analysis that changed a decision

prompt.text: **Tell us about an analysis you did that changed a decision, or should have.** What did you see, what did you do, and what would you do differently?
Specifics such as numbers and timelines matter more than polish.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.
